channel.title: Aditya Firmansyah — Field Notes
channel.description: Practitioner notes on software engineering, AI agents, and self-hosting. English and Bahasa Indonesia.

item.title: Secure CI/CD Pipeline Design: From GitHub Access to Production Data
item.description: A secure CI/CD pipeline must separate repository access from production authority. Here is how to reduce the blast radius when a developer account is compromised.

item.title: AI Coding Agent SSH Security Needs an Identity Boundary
item.description: AI coding agent SSH security depends on more than hiding private keys. Separate the agent’s identity and permissions from yours, then add key-use controls that fit the risk.

item.title: GitHub Actions YAML Parser: When the Runner and Linter Disagree
item.description: GitHub Actions YAML parser behavior can leave a security scan unable to read a workflow the runner accepts. Make parser compatibility and audit completion explicit CI gates.

item.title: AI-Generated Code Maintenance Is the Real Test of a Rust curl Rewrite
item.description: AI-generated code maintenance is the hard part of a Rust rewrite of curl. A convincing first build says little about compatibility, fixes, and releases a project must sustain.

item.title: Coding Agent Workflow: Build a Release Pipeline, Not a Better Prompt
item.description: A reliable coding agent workflow runs tests, records evidence, and requires human approval at meaningful risk boundaries. Better prompts help, but they do not prove a release is safe.

item.title: AI-Generated Code Open Source: What Should Teams Release?
item.description: AI-generated code open source is a debate about authorship and licensing, but engineering teams still need to review behavior, test boundaries, and choose deliberately what they publish.

item.title: Rust 1.100 Release: Why Dependency Cooldowns and Never Types Matter in Production
item.description: The Rust 1.100 release stabilizes Cargo dependency cooldowns, the canonical never type, and DropGuard. Here is what these operational upgrades mean for production backend reliability.

item.title: AWS Lambda Web Functions and the 7-Minute Idle Memory Tax
item.description: AWS Lambda Web Functions promised active CPU billing, but an unconfigurable 7-minute idle memory window drives 88% of compute costs for bursty, multi-tenant architectures.

item.title: AWS Emulator: 438 API Models, Zero Human-Written Code
item.description: AWS Emulator covers 438 AWS API models, and the commit log is all IssueFinderAgent and IssueFixerAgent. The harness did the work, not the model.

item.title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0: Why Chrome Skipped MCP to Stop Agents Writing 2019 JavaScript
item.description: Modern Web Guidance 1.0 ships 200+ browser-primitive guides as a 7MB offline CLI skill, and its rejection of MCP tells you more about AI coding agents than the guides do.

item.title: Expo Exact Framework: Native Apps With No React, No JSX
item.description: The Expo Exact framework drops React, JSX, and the JavaScript bridge, betting that a virtual clock and a ten-verb driver make native apps buildable by AI agents.

item.title: Agent Memory Doesn't Need a Schema, It Needs a Byte Budget
item.description: The push to standardize agent memory fixes the wrong layer. What actually degrades models is a store that never evicts, and a byte ceiling plus on-demand skills fixes it.

item.title: Claude Code Leaked Your Email Because a Website Asked Politely
item.description: A site asked for a contact address, and the agent handed over a real Gmail from its context window. The fix shows why a regex hook is not a security boundary.

item.title: Four Decades of Defensive Workarounds, One OpenSSH musl Password Bypass
item.description: How layered workarounds created the OpenSSH musl password bypass (*sshole) on Alpine Linux hosts, allowing long passwords to unlock accounts marked with an asterisk.

item.title: Zig's libc Rewrite Made SQLite 12,000x Slower. Your Tests Wouldn't Catch It
item.description: A cross-compiled Rust service lost 12,000x on SQLite inserts because Zig's libc rewrite walked the whole string inside every strchr call. Local tests passed on macOS.

item.title: What a Failed C++26 Ballot Says About Shipping to an Ecosystem
item.description: C++26's draft standard was reported disapproved in its ISO ballot over contracts. The useful question is what separates a feature that passes every internal gate from one an ecosystem can safely depend on.

item.title: The 46-vCPU Pod Trap: What PostHog Learned by Leaving DuckDB
item.description: PostHog ran DuckDB as a multi-tenant warehouse for five months, then scrapped it. The lesson is about where a single-node engine stops being a bargain.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Is Late Because Finding Bugs Got Cheap
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 slid to November 19 and lost three features late in beta. The cause is not worse code. Naming a defect got cheap while verifying one stayed human work.

item.title: Why Go 1.24's Default MPTCP Exposed Linux Hosts to CVE-2026-98432
item.description: Go 1.24 enabled Multipath TCP by default on Linux listeners, turning a subtle kernel Use-After-Free flaw into a remote root risk across unpatched servers.

item.title: Backdooring Claude Code on Cursor: Why IDE Extensions Must Be Sandboxed
item.description: An 11-hour breach of Cursor's marketplace proxy injected a reverse SSH backdoor into Claude Code. Developer tools cannot safely share an unsandboxed runtime with workstation credentials.
